preconditions.description: The input must be a string of arbitrary characters (including Unicode, whitespace, and non-printable).

postconditions.expression: all(isinstance(c, str) and len(c) == 1 for c in return_value)
postconditions.description: Every element in the output list is a single-character string.

postconditions.expression: len(return_value) == sum(1 for c in input if input.count(c) % 2 != 0)
postconditions.description: The output list contains exactly one entry per character that appears an odd number of times in the input string.

postconditions.expression: all(c in input for c in return_value)
postconditions.description: Every character in the output list exists in the input string.

postconditions.expression: all(input.rindex(c) == input.index(c) for c in return_value if input.count(c) == 1) and all(input.rindex(c) == input.rfind(c) for c in return_value)
postconditions.description: For characters appearing exactly once, their position in the output matches their position in the input. For characters appearing multiple times, the last occurrence in the input is chosen.

postconditions.expression: len(return_value) == 0 or return_value[-1] == input[-1] if input.count(input[-1]) % 2 != 0 else True
postconditions.description: If the last character of the input string appears an odd number of times, it must be the last element in the output list.
